source: Moss et al. (2013) Trusting Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Medical Data
text: Each patient has monitoring sessions. Each timepoint in a monitoring session is associated with observations produced by sensors. Each observation measures a physiological parameter and is evaluated by a data quality assessment resulting in either a Possible Error (PoE) or Probable Error (PrE) classification. A reading outside range may be contextualised by a medical disorder (e.g. sepsis, hypertension) or recent treatment (e.g. noradrenaline), reclassifying a PrE as PoE.

source: Decraene et al. (2023) Decompressive craniectomy as a second/third-tier intervention in TBI
text: One of the cornerstones of brain-protective strategies is to reduce and control intracranial pressure (ICP), thereby avoiding secondary ischemic damage. source: Güiza et al. (2015) Visualizing the Pressure and Time Burden of Intracranial Hypertension
text: An increased ICP is an independent risk factor for mortality, and the total burden of ICP derangements, calculated as the area under the ICP curve above 20 mmHg, is an independent predictor of worse outcome. The autoregulatory status has a major effect on the transition curves in both adults and children. When autoregulation is intact, the transition curve shifts to the right; with impaired autoregulation, there is a dramatic shift to the left suggesting higher vulnerability to raised ICP.
